observations: Photo 0 shows a chest freezer (upright lid) in white/grey body.
A label on the front panel in photo 0 reads '120 HOURS COOLING RETENTION'.
No brand/model name is clearly readable in photo 0.
No visible power-on test, thermometer reading, or running compressor sound is shown.
No clear capacity marking (e.g., 250L) is readable in photo 0.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 does not show a readable capacity marking.
No low-voltage spec is readable in photo 0.
Photo 0 label shows '120 HOURS COOLING RETENTION'.
Photo 0 shows the freezer but no power-on/running test.

claims.claim: Barely used, bought new last year. No fault at all, the motor was never opened. Receipt and warranty card available.
claims.evidence: No receipt/warranty card or evidence of motor not being opened is shown in photo 0.

risks.risk: Capacity may not be 250L (could be different size), affecting value.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of the rating/capacity plate (inside lid or rear) showing liters/model.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic used chest freezer with uncertain capacity.

risks.risk: May not be truly working (compressor/thermostat/relay issues not visible).
risks.proof: Ask for a short video of it plugged in and running (compressor sound + temperature drop after 10–15 minutes).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven working (worst case: treat as needing service).

risks.risk: Low-voltage performance may be overstated; it may trip or fail under Rivers power conditions.
risks.proof: Ask for a test clip showing it running on a low-voltage/unstable supply (or specify the voltage range on the label).
risks.if_unproven: Price as standard operation only (no guaranteed low-voltage tolerance).

risks.risk: Cooling retention claim may be marketing; actual performance could be lower due to insulation/gasket wear.
risks.proof: Ask for a temperature hold test (e.g., set to freeze, then unplug and show temperature over time).
risks.if_unproven: Price without assuming the 120-hour retention is achieved in real use.

risks.risk: Condition issues (dents, seal leaks, rust, missing parts) not fully visible from one angle.
risks.proof: Ask for close-up photos of the lid gasket/hinge, drain area, and corners/edges.

proof_requests: Photo of the freezer’s rating plate showing brand/model and exact capacity (liters).
Video of the freezer plugged in and running (compressor on) plus a thermometer reading after 10–15 minutes.
Close-up photos of the lid gasket and hinge, and the rear/side for any damage or missing parts.
Photo of receipt/warranty card (if available) or any serial number matching the plate.
response.reason: The photo supports only the '120 hours cooling retention' label; capacity, low-voltage capability, and working condition are not verifiable from the single image, so a confident price cannot be set without the key proof.
